vectors.description: fetch stream header (type 0x05) with one object (flags=0x1c: GROUP_ID_DELTA, OBJECT_ID_DELTA, PRIORITY all present; subgroup mode=0); first object's deltas are absolute values
fetch stream with two objects (Ascending group order); second uses pure delta encoding (flags=0x00) — Object ID is prior+1 within the same group

fetch stream where the second object starts a new group via GROUP_ID_DELTA (flags=0x0c: GROUP_ID_DELTA + OBJECT_ID_DELTA). In Ascending order, new Group ID = prior + delta + 1, and Object ID = Object ID Delta when Group ID Delta is present.

fetch stream where the second object carries an Object ID Delta but no Group ID Delta (flags 0x04). Section 11.4.4.1: "When the Group ID Delta field is not present, the Object ID is the prior Object's ID plus the Object ID Delta if present" — so this is prior + delta (0 + 4 = 4), not the delta itself, and not prior + delta + 1. The Group ID Delta present case one row above resolves Object ID differently, which is what makes this pair worth having: a decoder that reads Object ID Delta the same way in both branches passes one and fails the other

fetch stream where the second object starts a new group via Group ID Delta but carries no Object ID Delta (flags 0x08). Section 11.4.4.1: "If Object ID Delta is not present, the Object ID is the prior Object's ID plus one, regardless of which group it belongs to." So the Object ID continues 7 → 8 across the group boundary rather than restarting at 0, which is the reading a decoder is most likely to get wrong. Ascending order, so the Group ID is prior + delta + 1 = 1
fetch stream with End of Non-Existent Range marker (Serialization Flags=0x8C, encoded as 2-byte varint 0x808c); Group ID and Object ID fields are absolute values for this marker

fetch stream with first object carrying PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2 property (flags=0x3c: PROPERTIES+PRIORITY+GROUP_ID_DELTA+OBJECT_ID_DELTA), in Group 5. Section 12.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), so the Group ID is at least the gap
fetch stream with End of Unknown Range marker (Serialization Flags=0x10C, encoded as 2-byte varint 0x810c), group_id=5, object_id=10
fetch stream with DATAGRAM flag (flags=0x5c: DATAGRAM+PRIORITY+GROUP_ID_DELTA+OBJECT_ID_DELTA); two LSBs are ignored and no Subgroup ID is present
fetch stream with explicit subgroup_id (flags=0x1f: subgroup mode=0b11 present, PRIORITY+GROUP_ID_DELTA+OBJECT_ID_DELTA)

vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading request_id

vectors.description: fetch stream with Objects 0 and 1 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2 and 3. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 12.8: "A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2)
vectors.error_detail: two Objects in Group 5 carry different Prior Group ID Gap values

vectors.description: fetch stream with an object in Group 9 and then Object 0 of Group 10 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 (flags 0x2C; its Group ID Delta of 0 is the prior Group ID plus 1). Section 12.8: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Group ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." The gap covers Group 9, which this stream delivered first. Section 2.1: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Objects 8 and 9 of Group 3, the second carrying Prior Object ID Gap 1. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 12.9: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Object ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." Section 10.12.3: "Within each group, objects are sent in Object ID order; subgroup ID is not used for ordering." The gap covers Object 8, delivered just before. Section 2.1: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 1 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2. Section 12.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Group ID Gap 2 is larger than Group ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 1 of Group 3 carrying Prior Object ID Gap 2. Section 12.9: "An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Object ID Gap 2 is larger than Object ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 twice. Section 12.8: "An Object contains more than one instance of Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: an Object contains more than one Prior Group ID Gap
